subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which sub-cellular structure controls the activities of a eukaryotic cell and contains its genetic material?
questions.explain: The nucleus contains the chromosomes (DNA) and controls the cell's activities.

questions.q: In which sub-cellular structure does most aerobic respiration take place?
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of most reactions of aerobic respiration, releasing energy.

questions.q: Where in the cell does protein synthesis occur?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site where proteins are made (protein synthesis).

questions.q: A plant cell wall is made mainly of which substance, which provides support?
questions.explain: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose, giving the cell strength and support.

questions.q: Which feature is present in a bacterial (prokaryotic) cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.explain: Plasmids are small rings of DNA found in prokaryotic cells but not in animal cells.

questions.q: How does the size of a typical prokaryotic cell compare with a typical eukaryotic cell?
options: Prokaryotic cells are generally much smaller than eukaryotic cells
Prokaryotic cells are generally much larger than eukaryotic cells
They are always exactly the same size
Prokaryotic cells have no measurable size
questions.explain: Prokaryotic cells are typically only a few micrometres across, much smaller than eukaryotic cells.

questions.q: A cell is seen to have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole. What type of cell is it?
questions.explain: Chloroplasts, a cellulose cell wall and a permanent vacuole are all features of plant cells.

questions.q: Which equation correctly links magnification, image size and actual size?
questions.explain: Magnification is calculated by dividing the size of the image by the real (actual) size of the object.

questions.q: Compared with a light microscope, an electron microscope allows scientists to see smaller structures mainly because it has a higher what?
questions.explain: Electron microscopes have much higher resolution (and magnification) than light microscopes, revealing finer detail.

questions.q: What is meant by the resolution of a microscope?
options: The ability to distinguish between two points that are close together
The total number of cells that can be seen
How many times larger the image appears
questions.explain: Resolution is the smallest distance between two points at which they can still be seen as separate.

questions.q: A structure appears 5 mm long in an image taken at a magnification of ×100. What is its actual length?
questions.explain: Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 5 mm ÷ 100 = 0.05 mm = 50 µm.

questions.q: Enzymes are biological catalysts made from which type of molecule?
questions.explain: Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions without being used up themselves.

questions.q: The carbohydrase amylase breaks down starch into which product?
questions.explain: Amylase is a carbohydrase that breaks starch down into simple sugars such as maltose.

questions.q: Lipase enzymes break down lipids into which products?
questions.explain: Lipase digests lipids (fats) into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: What happens to an enzyme when it is heated well above its optimum temperature?
options: The active site changes shape and the enzyme is denatured
The enzyme turns into a substrate
The active site becomes more specific
questions.explain: High temperatures change the shape of the active site so the substrate no longer fits; the enzyme is denatured.

questions.q: In the 'lock and key' model, why can each enzyme usually only catalyse one type of reaction?
options: The substrate has a complementary shape to the enzyme's active site
All substrates fit into every enzyme equally well
The enzyme is used up during the reaction
Enzymes have no specific active site
questions.explain: Only a substrate with a complementary shape fits the active site, making enzymes specific.

questions.q: A protease enzyme in the stomach has an optimum pH of about 2. What would most likely happen to its rate of reaction if the pH were raised to 7?
options: The rate of reaction would decrease
The rate would stay exactly the same
The rate would keep increasing indefinitely
The enzyme would become a substrate
questions.explain: Moving away from the optimum pH changes the active site's shape, lowering the rate of reaction.

questions.q: Osmosis is best described as the movement of which particles across a partially permeable membrane?
questions.explain: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane, from a dilute to a more concentrated solution.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes diffusion?
options: Net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration
Movement of particles from a lower to a higher concentration using energy
Movement of water only across a membrane
Movement of particles that requires energy from respiration
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient and does not require energy.

questions.q: How does active transport differ from diffusion?
options: It moves substances against the concentration gradient using energy from respiration
It only ever moves water molecules
It always moves substances from high to low concentration
questions.explain: Active transport moves substances from a low to a high concentration, requiring energy from respiration.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Biology (1BI0) specification; Key Concepts in Biology
